summary: This article explains how tiny decomposers, worms, air, and water turn food scraps and dry leaves into rich compost that feeds plants and keeps food out of landfills.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “Composting: Turning Waste into Soil” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: a substance that living things need to grow and stay healthy
a large place where garbage is buried under the ground

challengeTerms.def: an organism that breaks down dead plants and animals into simpler substances
a colorless gas that traps heat in the atmosphere and can burn
a living thing so small that it can be seen only with a microscope

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that every home should compost its food scraps? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how to make good compost and why each step matters.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review nutrient, moist, and landfill, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use decomposer, methane, and microorganism in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
